answer: At a jetty market, agents pricing velvet falcon banners use a stake-weighted median of supplier quotes. Each quote locks collateral for the round; its weight equals that collateral, and no deposit can back two quotes. Splitting a stake among aliases preserves total weight. If honest quotes hold more than half the locked stake, fake accounts cannot push the median outside the honest price range. This prevents identity amplification, not majority-stake capture, and depends on honest suppliers quoting accurately.
